answer.rationale: The release must not be reverted (eliminates rollback). The write path is hot at settlement peak; p99 climbing 5x with heavy writes points to capacity/contention rather than a partner dependency (circuit breaker) or read pressure (read replicas). Failover could shift load cleanly per memory_b2 but is coarse and risky at peak if the issue isn't regional. memory_b3 shows provisioning headroom ahead of peak absorbed surges with flat queues—additive capacity is the lowest-blast-radius, customer-writes-preserving option. Verify memory_b3 (how headroom was provisioned and isolated from the write path) and memory_b2 (regional failover execution, as a fallback if capacity doesn't bite). Start with a small, guarded capacity add on the write path; if p99 doesn't recover in the next window, failover to the healthy region per memory_b2's pattern. Reads are not the issue, so don't route to replicas. If memory_b3 shows capacity adds previously coincided with regressions or required draining, adjust before scaling further.
